On the 1st (local time), President Trump announced in a national address that he would deliver a powerful blow to Iran over the next two to three weeks. As expectations for an end to the war between the U.S. and Iran have faded, uncertainty in the global economy is growing.

The government has prepared a supplementary budget of 26.2 trillion won to respond to the economic crisis spreading due to the aftermath of the situation in the Middle East.

We will take a closer look at the key details of the "2026 Supplementary Budget," also known as the "War Supplementary Budget."

snippet.description:
중동 상황 장기화에 따른 
국제 유가 상승으로 생필품 물가가 들썩이자 
정부가 외식비와 공공요금 등 
20개 품목을 추가 지정해 특별 관리합니다 

정부는 중동발 물가 파급이
1~3차에 걸쳐 단계적으로 
나타날 것으로 보고 있는데요

1차로는 에너지 품목, 
2차로 운송·물류 부문의 가격을 밀어 올리고
3차 파급은 공산품, 가공식품, 농축수산물과
외식 서비스까지 광범위하게 영향을 
미치게 될 것이란 판단입니다

정부는 총 43개 
특별 관리 대상 품목에 대해 
가격·수급 관리, 할인 지원, 불공정 거래 단속 등을
집중적으로 시행할 방침인데요

en-US.title: Addressing Instability in Consumer Prices Amidst Prolonged Middle East Situation! Energy, Logisti...
en-US.description:
As the prices of daily necessities fluctuate due to rising international oil prices resulting from the prolonged situation in the Middle East, the government has designated 20 additional items, including dining-out costs and public utility fees, for special management.

The government anticipates that the price ripple effects originating from the Middle East will manifest in stages, spanning three phases.

The assessment is that the first phase will push up prices in energy items, the second in the transportation and logistics sectors, and the third phase will broadly affect manufactured goods, processed foods, agricultural and fishery products, and even dining-out services.

The government plans to intensively implement measures such as price and supply management, discount support, and crackdowns on unfair trade practices for a total of 43 items subject to special management.

We examined the details with an expert.

en-US.title: “Women in their 30s are the main contributors.” January birth rate approaches 1.0! What is behind...
en-US.description:
Guest: Lee Jung-hwan, Associate Professor, School of Economics and Finance, Hanyang University

Last January, the number of births neared 27,000, marking a seven-year high, and the total fertility rate also approached 1.

The number of marriages, which serves as a leading indicator of childbirth, continued its upward trend, reaching a seven-year high.

This is being interpreted as a result reflecting the delay effect caused by COVID-19 and changes in the perceptions of young people.

Furthermore, it is reported that the government's support policies for work-family balance, including marriage and childbirth, are making a substantial contribution to the increase in marriage and birth rates.

We will discuss in detail the background of the rise in the birth rate, policies to address low birth rates, and the remaining challenges.

en-US.title: Government Forms 26.2 Trillion Won ‘War Supplementary Budget’... What Is the Purpose and Eligibil...
en-US.description:
The government is set to begin full-scale fiscal injections by formulating a supplementary budget of 26.2 trillion won to respond to the shock of high oil prices triggered by the worsening situation in the Middle East.

The government has allocated the largest portion, 10.1 trillion won, to the "alleviation of the burden of high oil prices" category.

While lowering the burden of fuel and transportation costs for all citizens, the plan is to provide oil price damage relief funds ranging from 100,000 to 600,000 won per person to the bottom 70% of income earners.

We examined the supplementary budget bill to overcome the Middle East crisis and the key details of the oil price damage relief funds, which are attracting the most attention, with an economic commentator.

en-US.title: Bio & Health Exports Reach All-Time High Last Year! Up 10.3% Year-on-Year, What Is the Competitiv...
en-US.description:
Guest: Jung Yoon-taek, President of the Pharmaceutical Industry Strategy Research Institute

Last year, exports from the domestic bio-health industry, including pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and cosmetics, reached a record high of $27.9 billion.

The government has designated the realization of becoming one of the top five bio-health powerhouses as a national agenda and is focusing on four key directions: a paradigm shift in bio-health, data-based AI healthcare, strengthening regional and essential medical services, and mission-oriented challenging research.

With the launch of the 'National Bio-Innovation Committee,' a pan-government control tower, last March, the implementation of bio-health policies—including R&D investment directions and regulatory improvements—is becoming more systematized.

We will take a detailed look at the current status and outlook of K-Bio, as well as government policies.
